text:
Noah Kim: Heads-up: I opened a docs PR to update the Optimize Toolkit guide with our new recommendation for adaptive batching and to add a quantization compatibility matrix. The PR also fixes an outdated internal link to /optimize/quant-profiles#compatibility (slug changed). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4621

Priya Singh: Thanks Noah. Can you summarize the user-facing change so I can add it to the changelog entry? Want to make sure we call out any breaking migration steps.

Noah Kim: TL;DR for changelog: (1) Recommend adaptive batch sizing (auto-tune on steady load) instead of fixed batch_size defaults; (2) Documented model/quantization combinations that are unsupported (e.g., int4 on some Llama variants) in a compatibility table; (3) Noted SDK param rename: `max_batch` -> `batch_cap` in the optimize SDK v0.9.0 (migration snippet included).

Evan Brooks: Related: the PR currently includes an SDK snippet where Python uses `max_batch=64` but JS example still shows `batch_cap: 64` (inverted). We should keep both consistent and show the migration mapping. Otherwise users copy/paste and get silent failures.

Noah Kim: Good catch. I pushed a commit to the branch that standardizes examples and adds a short migration snippet:
```python
# before (optimize v0.8.x)
from redwood.optimize import configure
configure(policy={"max_batch": 64, "cache_prefix": "app-A"})
# after (optimize v0.9.0+)
from redwood.optimize import configure
configure(policy={"batch_cap": 64, "cache_prefix": "app-A"})
```
and JS: 
```javascript
// before
optimize.configure({ policy: { max_batch: 64, cachePrefix: 'app-A' } })
// after
optimize.configure({ policy: { batch_cap: 64, cachePrefix: 'app-A' } })
```

Priya Singh: Please also add a short note about semantics: `batch_cap` caps the dynamically tuned batch size whereas `max_batch` was a hard cap that could cause unnecessary tail latency. That wording saved us from support tickets when we rolled this internally.

Noah Kim: Added that explanation and an example of how adaptive tuning ramps: small burst -> batch 8, steady state -> batch 48.

QA-bot: Linkcheck failed: /optimize/quant-profiles#compatibility returns 404 in preview due to anchor name change to #quant-compat. (checklink error in docs-ci).

Evan Brooks: I renamed the anchor in the compatibility table to `quant-compat` in the PR but missed the internal cross-link. I'll update the link and re-run preview. Also propose adding a table that shows tested combos: [model, quant, status, notes].

Priya Singh: For the compatibility matrix, can we add a short column that links to the evaluation run (s3/perf-reports/quant-eval-2026-01)? Users will want to see regressed quality numbers for int4. If that's sensitive, link to an internal read-only report instead.

Noah Kim: Good idea. I'll add a public summary link and keep raw logs internal. Also adding a small FAQ entry: "Why is int4 unsupported on model X?" with the short reasoning.

Evan Brooks: One more: docs CI flagged the new Playground embed (live sample) as blocked by CSP on staging. If we want a live interactive sample for adaptive batching, we either host as static runnable snippet or use the sandbox iframe we already approve. Flagging to docs-ops to review CSP.

docs-ops: Noted. We can host a static runnable example under /examples/optimize/adaptive-batching-demo.html and add CSP exception for the docs domain. Will file infra ticket.

Priya Singh: For release notes, recommend: "Optimize Toolkit: adaptive batch tuning is now recommended default; SDK param rename `max_batch` -> `batch_cap`; compatibility table for quantized models added." Add migration snippet link to the release notes.

Noah Kim: Done. I also added a small regression test in docs-ci that validates the examples compile: `python -m py_compile examples/optimize/*.py` and `node --check examples/optimize/*.js`. Keeps copy/paste from breaking the build.

QA-bot: docs-ci: tests failed initially due to the JS example still using `max_batch` in two places. Tests pass after Evan's fix.

Evan Brooks: Fixed and squashed. Requesting a docs review from @Priya and @docs-ops.

Priya Singh: Reviewing now. Please also add a short migration note in /contrib/migrations.md and link it from the guide.

Noah Kim: Added migration note and linked it. Ready to merge after Priya review.

Priya Singh: Approved. Merge when green. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

QA-bot: Merge queued by Priya Singh 1:03 UTC.

Noah Kim: Thanks everyone. After merge I'll follow up with a small customer-facing blurb for the dashboard release notes so Support can pre-empt questions. "If you rely on fixed batch sizes, expect reduced tail latency when switching to adaptive tuning."
